overview: Duolingo is the world's leading mobile learning platform, offering language learning in 40+ languages alongside Math, Music, and Chess through a gamified, freemium app. As of Q1 2026 the company had 56.5 million daily active users (DAUs), 12.5 million paid subscribers, and generated $1.037 billion in FY2025 revenue — its first billion-dollar year. The company has declared 2026 an 'investment year,' deliberately compressing margins to ~26% Adjusted EBITDA while targeting 100 million DAUs over the medium term, accepting near-term financial deceleration to build a larger monetizable base.

business_model.summary: Freemium model with approximately 86% of Q1 2026 revenue from subscriptions, supplemented by advertising (7%), Duolingo English Test (4%), and in-app purchases (3%). FY2025 delivered $1.037B revenue (+39% YoY) and $1.158B bookings (+33% YoY) with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 29.5%. For FY2026, the company is deliberately moderating margins to ~26% to reinvest in user growth, AI content, and product quality — a strategic trade-off of near-term EBITDA for long-term platform durability. The three-tier subscription structure (Free, Super at ~$7/month, Max at ~$14/month) allows monetization across the willingness-to-pay spectrum.
business_model.customer_type: B2C (individual learners globally), with institutional use via Duolingo for Schools (COPPA/FERPA compliant) and B2B via Duolingo English Test accepted at 6,100+ programs
business_model.geographic_mix: North and Latin America ~55%, Europe/Middle East/Africa ~32%, Asia-Pacific ~13% (based on IAP revenue data); Asia is fastest-growing region with China now achieving profitable performance marketing unit economics

main_competitors: PolyChat and other AI-native language apps
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in language learning apps by virtually every metric. FY2025 revenue of $1.037B dwarfs Babbel's ~$270M. #1 grossing app in Education on both Google Play and Apple App Store. Most downloaded language app globally with an order-of-magnitude DAU lead over nearest app competitors. Over 6,100 educational institutions accept Duolingo English Test.

moat_factors.description: Over 10 million users maintain streaks of 1+ years. Daily check-in habit makes Duolingo uniquely sticky vs. passive AI chatbots. Streak mechanics and social features (leaderboards, friend streaks) drive engagement that competitors cannot easily replicate.

Iconic owl mascot and 'unhinged' social media strategy make Duolingo one of the most recognized edtech brands globally. Named Marketer of the Year by AdAge. Organic word-of-mouth is the primary user acquisition channel — a significant cost advantage.

moat_factors.factor: Data flywheel and AI content advantage
moat_factors.description: Billions of learning sessions generate proprietary data enabling personalized AI instruction. AI now allows 20,500 course units published per quarter in Q1 2026, up from 7,100/quarter in 2025 and 1,800/quarter in 2024 — a 10x acceleration in content velocity that widens the course library moat.

Robust free experience attracts 133M+ MAUs, creating an enormous top-of-funnel that converts to paid (12.5M subscribers = ~9.4% DAU-to-paid penetration). This scale is structurally difficult for competitors to replicate.

Expansion into Chess (fastest-growing subject), Math, and Music positions Duolingo as a broader daily learning platform, not just a language app. Chess growing fastest of any new subject ever launched.

weaknesses: DAU growth decelerating from 49% (Q1 2025) to 21% (Q1 2026); the 'top-of-funnel' described as 'about flat' in Q1 2026 earnings call
Bookings growth decelerating sharply — 33% in FY2025, guided to only 10.5% in FY2026, and just ~6% guided for Q2 2026
Max tier migration risk: Video Call feature is reportedly migrating from the premium Max tier toward the broader Super subscriber base, pressuring ARPU in the near term
Dependency on Apple and Google app stores for distribution and payments (15-30% platform take rates)
Gross margin drifting lower as AI costs rise — guided from 73% in Q1 2026 to approximately 69% by Q4 2026 as more AI features embed into the product
Effectiveness ceiling debate: research suggests typical users plateau at A2-B1 (elementary/lower-intermediate), limiting retention of advanced learners

growth_drivers: AI-accelerated content creation: publishing 20,500 course units per quarter in Q1 2026 (vs. 1,800/quarter in 2024), enabling deeper courses at CEFR B2 level across 9 core languages and faster expansion of Chess, Math, and Music

Speaking and conversation features: Spoken Tokens, Speaking Adventures, and Flashcards added to free and paid tiers; Video Call users speaking 2x more words per session YoY — building toward a genuine conversation-practice moat

Duolingo Max AI tier: premium $14/month tier with Video Call, Roleplay, and Explain My Answer (powered by GPT-4); Max penetration growing from ~5% to ~9% of paid base over the past year; longer-term monetization lever as the feature set deepens

International expansion, particularly Asia: China achieving profitable performance marketing unit economics; English learners in China, India, Japan, and Korea represent the largest global language-learning demand pool and are underrepresented in current revenue

Duolingo English Test (DET) growth: accepted at 6,100+ institutions including 24 of the top 25 U.S. undergraduate programs by international enrollment; generated $11.3M in Q1 2026, expanding B2B revenue line

User growth flywheel: deliberate 2026 investment in free-tier experience quality to drive organic word-of-mouth DAU growth toward 100M medium-term target; content velocity improvements reduce ARPU pressure from reduced monetization friction
Adjacent subjects as daily utility: Chess fastest-growing subject ever; Math and Music broaden daily app utility and open new user acquisition cohorts outside language learners
$400M share buyback program (no expiration) authorized alongside growth investments, providing capital return optionality against a $1.036B cash balance with no debt

business.description: DAU growth slowed from 49% (Q1 2025) to 21% (Q1 2026), and top-of-funnel new user acquisition is described as 'about flat.' Bookings growth decelerated from 33% (FY2025) to 14% (Q1 2026) to just ~6% guided for Q2 2026. The 2026 investment strategy of reducing monetization friction is creating a near-term bookings air pocket with no guarantee of DAU re-acceleration.

ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and AI-native language apps (PolyChat, etc.) offer free or low-cost conversational practice. Duolingo's own 'AI-first' declaration acknowledges the competitive threat. Studies suggest Duolingo users plateau at A2-B1, opening a gap that AI tutors can fill. The race to 100M DAUs is partly a race to lock in habits before AI alternatives become ubiquitous.

Management is reportedly testing migration of Video Call (core Max feature) to the broader Super tier, which could reduce the differentiation and pricing power of the $14/month Max tier. This would compress revenue per subscriber even as subscriber count grows.
Reliance on Apple and Google app stores for distribution and in-app purchase processing (15-30% take rates). Subject to platform policy changes.

financial.risk: Gross margin compression from AI costs
financial.description: Gross margin guided to decline from 73.0% (Q1 2026) to approximately 69% by Q4 2026 as AI-powered features (Video Call, Speaking Adventures, personalized content generation) scale. Variable AI API costs grow with Max adoption and content generation volume. This is a structural change, not a temporary headwind.

Adjusted EBITDA margin guided at ~25.7% for FY2026, down from 29.5% in FY2025. Q2 2026 margin guided to trough at ~24%. The original FY2026 EBITDA guidance of ~$302M (Feb 2026) has since been raised slightly to ~$310M at Q1 2026 earnings (May 2026), but still represents a significant compression from prior-year levels.

Over 50% of bookings from outside the US. USD strength creates headwind to reported bookings and revenue. Q2 2026 bookings guidance in constant currency (4.1%) is materially softer than reported (5.8%).
Stock-based compensation rising to ~15% of revenue in FY2026 (from 13% in FY2025), with net share count dilution of 3.5-4% expected. The $400M buyback partially offsets gross dilution.

regulatory.description: Collects voice, biometric, and behavioral data from hundreds of millions of users including children. GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, and FERPA compliance obligations. Emerging AI regulations (EU AI Act) may impose restrictions on AI-generated educational content and data used for model training.
Targeting English learners in China (achieving profitable unit economics) but subject to unpredictable regulatory approvals, content restrictions, and data localization requirements.

EU Digital Markets Act and US regulatory action on Apple/Google could alter distribution economics, potentially improving Duolingo's margin (lower take rates) or disrupting existing revenue recognition patterns.

macro.description: Premium subscriptions ($7-14/month) are discretionary but low-ticket. Education is relatively recession-resistant, and Duolingo's free tier provides a buffer. Conversion rates may soften in a downturn but churn risk is limited by streak and habit mechanics.

At ~$120/share (June 2026), DUOL trades at approximately 10x FY2026 revenue and ~39x FY2026 Adj. EBITDA on a $5.6B market cap. For a company with 15-18% revenue growth and declining margins, this is a premium multiple. A 36% YoY EPS decline expected in Q2 2026 could pressure valuation further.

execution.description: New CFO Gillian Munson (joined February 23, 2026, former Vimeo CFO and Duolingo board Audit Committee Chair) is navigating her first full year of guidance-setting during a deliberate strategy reset. Matt Skaruppa, who led the IPO and profitability scaling, remains in an advisory role through the transition.

The company has explicitly prioritized DAU growth and teaching quality over near-term monetization in 2026. If DAU growth does not re-accelerate materially despite the reduction in monetization friction, management loses both the growth narrative and the margin, leaving the stock with no near-term catalyst. As of Q1 2026, top-of-funnel is 'about flat,' making this risk live.

Chess, Math, and Music are scaling but remain early-stage. Replicating language learning's virality and retention in non-language subjects is unproven at scale. Failure to diversify subjects would keep Duolingo a language-learning company facing a maturing core market.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Online language learning market valued at ~$22B in 2026, projected to reach $94B by 2035 (18% CAGR per Business Research Insights). AI integration is the dominant industry trend, both as a threat (free AI tutors) and enabler (personalized, conversational learning at scale). Duolingo is positioned at the intersection, using AI offensively while facing AI substitution risk defensively. Broader edtech market growing as mobile and lifelong learning behaviors solidify globally.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low cyclicality. Education is resilient, and Duolingo's $7-14/month price points are low relative to disposable income. Free tier with ads provides a fully functional product that buffers churn in downturns. App store habits are stickier than most consumer discretionary categories.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity. Growth stock valuation is sensitive to rates — the stock declined from $544 peak (May 2025) to a low of ~$88 (early 2026), a ~84% decline, driven by both growth deceleration concerns and rate/risk appetite dynamics. Stock has partially recovered to ~$120 as of June 2026.
key_input_costs: Generative AI API costs (OpenAI GPT-4 for Max features)
Content creation (AI-assisted, but still requires editorial oversight)
Stock-based compensation (~15% of revenue in FY2026)

recent_developments.event: DUOL stock fell 9.24% on June 25, 2026, underperforming broader market. As of June 26-27, 2026, stock trades near $120-121, with a 52-week range of $87.89 to $468.00. Market cap approximately $5.6-6.2B. Motley Fool published 'The Duolingo Rally Is Finally Starting' (June 26, 2026), noting a ~20% monthly recovery driven by Q1 beat and investor re-rating.

Q1 2026 earnings reported. Revenue $292M (+27% YoY, beat $289M guide), Bookings $308.5M (+14% YoY), Adj. EBITDA $83.4M (28.6% margin, beat), Gross margin 73.0% (+190bps YoY). DAUs 56.5M (+21% YoY), Paid subscribers 12.5M (+21% YoY). Stock dropped 13.9% on Q2 bookings guidance miss ($283.5M, +6% YoY). Full-year guidance maintained at $1.205B revenue and $1.28B bookings; Adj. EBITDA slightly raised to $310M (from ~$302M prior guidance midpoint).

CEO Luis von Ahn commentary on Q1 2026 call: 'We said we were going to prioritize teaching better and growing users, and that's exactly what we did.' Announced AI content velocity of 20,500 course units in Q1 alone (vs. 7,100/quarter average in 2025, 1,800/quarter in 2024) — a 10x acceleration in two years. Described potential for fully AI-generated personalized content tailored to individual users.

New product features announced or expanded: Spoken Tokens (gamified speaking exercises available broadly), Speaking Adventures (real-world conversational scenarios), and Flashcards added to free and paid tiers. Video Call feature reported as migrating from Max tier toward Super subscriber base. Users of Video Call speaking 2x more words per session vs. prior year.

Q4 and FY2025 earnings reported. Revenue $1.037B (+39% YoY), Bookings $1.158B (+33% YoY), Adj. EBITDA margin 29.5%, FCF $360.4M. DAUs 52.7M (+30% YoY), Paid subscribers 12.2M (+28% YoY). FY2026 guidance issued: Revenue $1.197-1.221B (+15-18%), Bookings $1.274-1.298B (+10-12%), Adj. EBITDA ~25% margin — all well below analyst consensus. Stock fell 22.5% to intraday low of $91.61.

Board authorized $400M share repurchase program with no expiration date — Duolingo's first capital return program. Company holds $1.036B in cash and no debt, funding both buybacks and growth investment simultaneously.
New CFO Gillian Munson (former Vimeo CFO, ex-Duolingo Audit Committee Chair) officially started just days before the consequential FY2025 earnings release. Matt Skaruppa moved to advisory role.

Q3 2025 results: DAUs 50.5M (+36% YoY), Revenue $271.7M (+41% YoY), Adj. EBITDA margin 29.5%. Company first formally announced strategic shift toward user growth over near-term monetization at this earnings release.
Stock peaked at all-time high of $544.93 (May 14, 2025), representing a ~67% YTD gain. Stock has since declined approximately 78% from that peak to current levels (~$120).

CEO Luis von Ahn announced 'AI-first' company strategy via companywide email, stating Duolingo would replace contractors with AI. Public backlash required partial walkback, but signaled the company's strategic commitment to AI-driven content and product development.

items.notes: +15-18% YoY growth. Q1 actual of $292M (+27%) came in ahead of the $288.5M Q1 guide, but full-year guidance was not raised despite the beat, reflecting confidence in the bookings deceleration trajectory.

+10-12% (10.5%) YoY growth, a sharp deceleration from +33% in FY2025. Q1 actual bookings of $308.5M (+14%) beat the $301.5M Q1 guide, but full-year bookings guidance was not raised — management is pulling back monetization friction across the year.

Margin expected to trough in Q2 and recover through H2, with Q4 being highest-margin quarter. Compression vs. FY2025's 29.5% driven by faster opex growth, higher AI costs, and increased marketing spend.
Similar to FY2025's $360.4M. FCF more resilient than EBITDA due to working capital dynamics including deferred revenue.
+17.1% YoY growth. Revenue guide is less controversial than bookings since bookings lead revenue by 1-2 quarters.

Lowest quarter of FY2026. Reflects peak investment in AI content, marketing, and product. Recovery expected in H2.

items.target: ~71% in Q2 2026, drifting to ~69% by Q4 2026
items.notes: Structural pressure from expanding AI-powered features (Video Call, Speaking Adventures, personalized content generation). Not expected to recover near-term as AI feature scope widens.
Top-of-funnel new user acquisition described as 'about flat' in Q1 2026. Long-term 100M DAU target not time-bound but CEO has referenced 2028 as a target horizon.
Absolute dollar increase reflects incremental hiring for AI, product, and marketing initiatives.
Gross SBC dilution partially offset by $400M buyback program. No expiration on buyback authorization.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Luis von Ahn on Q1 2026 call: 'We said we were going to prioritize teaching better and growing users, and that's exactly what we did. We may even start generating content just for you — based on everything we know about you, we may just be able to generate content just for you.' On AI content velocity: published 20,500 course units in Q1 2026 alone, more than 10 times what was published in a single quarter two years ago. CFO Gillian Munson on margin: Q2 will be the trough, with recovery through H2; gross margin will drift from 73% to approximately 69% by Q4 as AI features expand. On the 100M DAU target: CEO von Ahn has referenced a 2028 target horizon, requiring a re-acceleration to ~26% average DAU growth in 2027-2028 from the current ~21%.

bull_case: AI-powered content flywheel is a structural moat: 20,500 course units published in Q1 2026 alone (10x the 2024 pace) means Duolingo's app depth and personalization is pulling away from every human-curated competitor. No other language app has the data scale or AI infrastructure to close this gap quickly.

FY2026 investment cycle mirrors successful 2022-2023 playbook: Duolingo has deliberately cycled through margin compression before (2022-2023) and emerged with dramatically accelerated DAU growth. Bulls see 2026 as a reset that positions the company for re-acceleration in 2027-2028 as the larger, better-quality free experience converts more users organically.

100M DAU target is a compelling long-duration growth story: at 56.5M DAUs and 12.5M paid subscribers (~22% penetration), there is substantial room to grow. If DAUs reach 100M at current paid penetration and ARPU, revenue would roughly double. The free-product quality investment thesis is: better teaching → more word-of-mouth → faster DAU growth → more monetization.

Balance sheet strength and capital return optionality: $1.036B cash, no debt, >$350M FCF guided for FY2026, and $400M buyback program (active, no expiration) provide substantial downside protection and shareholder return capacity at current valuation levels.

Valuation reset may be excessive: stock at ~$120 trades at ~10x FY2026 revenue on a $5.6B market cap — a 78% decline from the May 2025 peak — reflecting the full weight of guidance disappointment. Analyst consensus retains a Buy bias with price targets in the $145-225 range, implying 20-90% upside from current levels. TIKR model targets $209.
bear_case: Top-of-funnel is 'about flat' while bookings growth is collapsing to 6% in Q2 2026: the 2026 strategy — sacrifice monetization to grow users — is not yet showing DAU re-acceleration, meaning the company currently has neither the growth nor the margins. This is the most dangerous near-term setup.

Gross margin is structurally eroding: the guided drift from 73% (Q1 2026) to ~69% (Q4 2026) is driven by AI feature costs that scale with the product roadmap, not a one-time item. As Video Call, Speaking Adventures, and personalized content generation expand, the AI cost base grows with them. Duolingo's business model may be permanently higher-cost than its 2022-2024 era.

AI substitution risk is not priced in as a structural threat: free AI tutors (ChatGPT, Gemini) are improving rapidly at exactly the conversational practice that Duolingo's Max tier charges a premium for. If the $14/month Max tier's Video Call feature migrates to the free Super tier to compete, ARPU collapses. If AI chatbots solve the A2-B1 plateau problem for free, Duolingo's advanced-user retention deteriorates.

Bookings leading indicator signals sustained deceleration: Q2 2026 bookings guided to just +6% (and +4% constant currency), which will flow into revenue with a 1-2 quarter lag. Even if H2 2026 shows bookings recovery, the revenue line remains under pressure into early 2027. Analysts currently model a 36% YoY EPS decline in Q2 2026.

Valuation remains elevated for the business fundamentals: at ~$120 and ~$5.6B market cap, DUOL trades at ~10x FY2026 revenue and ~39x FY2026 Adj. EBITDA. For a company guiding 10-12% bookings growth, compressing margins, and flat top-of-funnel, this multiple requires near-perfect execution on the long-term DAU thesis to justify. Any further guidance miss or DAU disappointment risks a renewed de-rating.
